Points F1 and F2 lie on side BC, with F1 closer to B and F2 closer to C. Points G2 and G1 lie on side AC, with G2 closer to A and G1 closer to C. The central hexagon is E1E2F1F2G1G2, and the three remaining corner regions are triangles AE1G2, BF1E2, and CG1F2. Reasoning: The central polygon E1E2F1F2G1G2 together with the three corner triangles AE1G2, BF1E2, and CG1F2 exactly partitions the whole equilateral triangle ABC. By the given equalities, each corner triangle has two sides of length m meeting at a 60-degree angle, since each corner is a vertex angle of the equilateral triangle. Therefore the area of each corner triangle is (1/2)m^2 sin 60° = (√3/4)m^2. The combined area of the three corner triangles is 3√3 m^2/4. The whole equilateral triangle ABC has side length M, so its area is √3 M^2/4. The problem states that the central polygon area equals the combined corner-triangle area. Since the total area is central area plus combined corner area, the combined corner area is half the total area. Thus 3√3 m^2/4 = √3 M^2/8. Canceling √3 gives 3m^2/4 = M^2/8, so 6m^2 = M^2. Hence m/M = 1/√6 = √6/6.

Image description: The diagram shows an equilateral triangle ABC. Points E1 and E2 lie on side AB, with E1 closer to A and E2 closer to B. Points F1 and F2 lie on side BC, with F1 closer to B and F2 closer to C. Points G2 and G1 lie on side AC, with G2 closer to A and G1 closer to C. The central hexagon is E1E2F1F2G1G2, and the three remaining corner regions are triangles AE1G2, BF1E2, and CG1F2.

Reasoning: The central polygon E1E2F1F2G1G2 together with the three corner triangles AE1G2, BF1E2, and CG1F2 exactly partitions the whole equilateral triangle ABC. By the given equalities, each corner triangle has two sides of length m meeting at a 60-degree angle, since each corner is a vertex angle of the equilateral triangle. Therefore the area of each corner triangle is (1/2)m^2 sin 60° = (√3/4)m^2. The combined area of the three corner triangles is 3√3 m^2/4. The whole equilateral triangle ABC has side length M, so its area is √3 M^2/4. The problem states that the central polygon area equals the combined corner-triangle area. Since the total area is central area plus combined corner area, the combined corner area is half the total area. Thus 3√3 m^2/4 = √3 M^2/8. Canceling √3 gives 3m^2/4 = M^2/8, so 6m^2 = M^2. Hence m/M = 1/√6 = √6/6.
